children: Cisco Systems reported better-than-expected results for its fiscal first quarter and lifted its outlook for the rest of the year, but investors are questioning whether it can keep up the momentum.
Artificial intelligence continues to be the moneymaker for Cisco, which makes networking solutions for businesses and data centers. It hasn't been this hot a stock since the dot-com bubble.
Cisco stock jumped in after-hours trading Thursday before falling 5.4% to $96.47 on Friday. Shares are up about 27% on the year, but have stagnated since mid-May.

The company reported adjusted earnings of $1.40 a share for the quarter, up from $1 last year and above analysts' consensus estimate of $1.33, per FactSet. Revenue surged 24% year over year to $18.5 billion, surpassing Wall Street's call for $18.1 billion.

Orders from big cloud-service providers are helping drive Cisco's growth. The company expects AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to hit $9 billion in fiscal 2027, more than double last year's total.
"We are in the very early stages of a multi-year networking supercycle," CEO Chuck Robbins said.

All told, Cisco expects adjusted earnings per share between $5.47 and $5.53 for the fiscal year on revenue of $75.3 billion at the midpoint. The company had previously guided for adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.11 a share.
The years beyond 2027 are less certain, though, according to William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji. The firm reiterated a Market Perform rating on Cisco stock in a research note Friday.

"Uneven hyperscaler spending and the eventual normalization of enterprise demand could make current growth rates difficult to sustain," Naji wrote, adding that a shift to more hardware-intensive business could weigh on profit margins.

Cisco's adjusted gross margin was 65.6% in the fiscal first quarter, down from 68.1% a year ago. A similar decline in margins weighed on Cisco stock last quarter. The rising cost of components used in AI hardware, like memory chips, was a key culprit.

Product order growth decelerated to 21% year over year in the quarter from 35% the prior two quarters. Order growth can slow without a corresponding dip in revenue growth for several quarters, says Ben Reitzes, an analyst at Melius Research. But investors would rather see the two numbers grow in tandem.
Reitzes reiterated a Buy rating and a $160 price target on Cisco stock.

The earnings report capped off an eventful week for Cisco after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday. The two companies have a partnership, with Cisco providing hardware to help connect Nvidia AI chips and servers.
